name: Aladdin
notes: Rebranded from Aladdin Mediterranean Cuisine to Maisa Lebanese Cuisine in 2026, same address/location (3900 Vermont St / suite address 1220 Cleveland Ave M101, San Diego, Hillcrest, 92103 - a corner retail complex with two street addresses); confirmed via news article and address match, not a different business. Prices on the restaurant's own Wix site (maisahillcrest.com/menus) matched the restaurant's own Toast online-ordering catalog (__OO_STATE__) to the cent across all 142 items, so treated as trusted per the 3PO precedent even though cent values are non-round (e.g. $9.28, $14.85) - a stale MenuPages listing (different item set including items no longer on the menu) showed round dollar/quarter prices for some overlapping-sounding items but did not match current item names, so it was judged an old/outdated snapshot and not used to override the two agreeing first-party sources. Sections covered: Appetizers, Soup, Salads, Wraps, Entrees, Meza Platter, Traditional Dishes, Sides and Extras, Desserts, Beverages, Beer, Glass of Wine, Bottles of Wine - matches the full section list shown on the Wix menu tabs, no core section appears missing.

notes: not_found: United Club is a members/day-pass airport lounge with all-inclusive complimentary food (breakfast buffet, lunch/afternoon buffet with soups, salads, sandwiches, cheeses, snacks, desserts) and complimentary standard beer/wine/spirits included with entry -- no per-item menu prices are published anywhere. Only premium top-shelf liquor and wine carry an extra charge, and no priced list of those was found; this matches the playbook's explicit 'lounge with all-inclusive food' not-found example.

name: Meraki Café
notes: DoorDash marketplace listing (server-rendered schema.org Menu JSON-LD, not the order.online white-label) with address matching the work list exactly (1735 Adams Avenue, San Diego). 59 dishes across 11 sections (Coffee, Not Coffee, Signature Drinks, Fresh Smoothies, Artisan Sandwiches, Breakfast, Bagels, Small Plates, Avocado Toast, Acai Bowls, Salads) reads as a complete cafe menu. Markup test on the ~11 non-whole-dollar prices found no consistent divisor. A SinglePlatform listing (places.singleplatform.com/meraki-cafe-0/menu) carries lower prices on overlapping items (e.g. Classic Acai $7.00 vs $10.00, Fresh Mozzarella sandwich $7.50 vs $11.00, Arugula Greek Salad $8.00 vs $11.00) at an inconsistent ratio (1.33x-1.47x) rather than a clean single markup factor -- per playbook this reads as SinglePlatform being a stale, restaurant-submitted, years-old price sheet rather than DoorDash carrying a fee, so SinglePlatform was not used as crossCheckedAgainst. Own site (merakicafesd.com) is a client-rendered GoDaddy builder page with no static menu content, and its Square Online ordering storefront (merakicafesd.square.site) fetches its catalog client-side with no prices in static HTML or __BOOTSTRAP_STATE__ -- would need a browser.

Business appears on delivery platforms as 'LIV Juice Bar and Smoothies' at the same address (1251 University Avenue) as the work-list entry, confirming same business under a name variant. Used DoorDash marketplace schema.org Menu JSON-LD (server-rendered, tier 3). Markup test (1.04/1.1/1.15/1.2/1.25) run across all 71 items found no consistent divisor pattern - passes. Sections reached: Tortas, Sandwiches, Soups & Salads, Bowls, Extras (add-ons), Boost (supplements), Raw Juices, Fruit Smoothies, Shots - a 'Most Ordered' 10th section was dropped as a duplicate sample of the others, not a distinct menu. All core categories for a juice-bar-and-breakfast concept (juices, smoothies, bowls, sandwiches, salads, soups) are present; nothing looks missing. Uniform $9.57 across all 27 raw-juice/smoothie items is unusual but internally consistent (odd non-round cents, not a farm tell like a clean $X.95); WebSearch summary of the same DoorDash-family listing independently reported matching prices for overlapping items (Breakfast Burrito-type $14 bowls, $9.57 smoothies).
